races.name: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with three wins and five places from 15 starts on similar Going, recording its sole win at this trip and course combination; David O'Meara in solid recent form (8/52 14-day), 10 days fresh, tongue-tie noted — suits uncontested lead but style-fit tag is only relevant if pushed back, which is unlikely here given the absence of true pace rivals.
runners_data.comment: Sixtygeesbaby arrives on the back of a win last time out, returning quickly on ten days' rest and having already encountered today's trip and conditions; rated 78 and ranked top of six here, he makes a compelling case, though the patchy nature of his other recent efforts gives the main cause for caution.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Three wins over 6f on Good ground make it the most credible hold-up challenger, and Rod Millman's 0/19 14-day strike rate is a dampener on confidence; 17 days since last run, Finley Marsh deputising — needs an honest pace it is unlikely to get in this small field to produce its trademark late finish.
runners_data.comment: Safari Dream won last time out and has previous experience over today's trip and going, making conditions familiar; he carries 137 lb from stall four and, with two wins in his last six starts, arrives in solid heart just 17 days after that success.

runners_data.name: Army Bugler
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's 3-year-old steps back up to 6f where it was beaten a head last time, the natural trip extension playing to its strengths; Harry Vigors (5lb claimer) takes off useful weight, and a prominent racing style means it should sit close enough to pounce if Sixtygeesbaby weakens — p headgear noted.
runners_data.comment: Army Bugler brings distance and going experience to this, and his our rating of 78 ranks him second in the field, giving him solid claims; the worry is that he has been sixth and seventh in his last two starts, so a return to the form that saw him win four starts back is the key.

runners_data.name: Alkuwarrior
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan pilots this hold-up 3-year-old whose sole win came on Soft over 5f, raising questions about whether Good ground and 6f are ideal; Christopher Mason has 1/6 in 14 days and the horse finished 14th last time over this trip — needs a big step forward against more experienced rivals.
runners_data.comment: Alkuwarrior won four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with a speed rating of 76 supporting his claims from stall one carrying 133 lb; the risk is that his last three outings have brought a pair of fifths and a seventh, so he must recapture that winning form.

runners_data.name: Liosa
runners_data.note: In-form on paper with a recent third and a win at this course and trip in its recent history, and trainer Zoe Hawkins has modest numbers; although naturally a prominent racer, the race shape pushes it back from its preferred position — it may try to race up with Sixtygeesbaby but securing that spot against a confirmed front-runner from a cold yard (0/2 14-day) looks tough.
runners_data.comment: Ranked fifth of six on our figures, Liosa is hard to fancy at these weights carrying 132 lb, and his recent form is patchy — sixth and fourth in the two starts before a win, though he does return in fair time and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type that the pace map has placed in midfield, reflecting a field with more come-from-behind horses than the shape can accommodate at the rear; Grace Harris has 2/19 14-day, and 0 wins from 5 recent starts alongside a bottom weight of 130lbs suggests this lightly-raced 3-year-old needs significant improvement to feature.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Pull The Rug faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a runner-up finish last time out — just 15 days ago — at least suggests she returns in reasonable heart.

races.paceDynamic: Sixtygeesbaby is the confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no serious pressure for the lead — with Liosa and Pull The Rug both true prominent/hold-up types who are mapped back from their natural positions due to the field's overall pace composition, Sixtygeesbaby can dictate at a comfortable, measured gallop. That uncontested lead on Good ground over 6f at Ffos Las creates a classic scenario where the pace-setter controls tempo without burning energy fighting for position, making the fractions less likely to be honest enough to bring back-markers into play late. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Liosa is the most likely of the displaced runners to push forward, but Sixtygeesbaby's head start in role suitability makes it hardest to dislodge. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers and front-runners who travel comfortably in the first two, with genuine hold-up horses facing the dual problem of a potentially moderate gallop and a tight 6-runner field leaving little cover or room to produce a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sixtygeesbaby Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Sixtygeesbaby bowls along uncontested in front and sets a sustainable, controlled tempo that the small field never truly tests.
scenarios.body: Sixtygeesbaby dictates every yard on Good ground at a trip and course it has demonstrated form over, and the proximity of the small field means no sustained pressure materialises until too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late-Early
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just hot enough midrace that Sixtygeesbaby ties up inside the final furlong and a prominent tracker swoops.
scenarios.body: Army Bugler, racing off the pace of the leader, is well-suited to a 6f trip having stepped up from 5f with a win and a second, and could pick up the pieces if Sixtygeesbaby over-commits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If Sixtygeesbaby goes too fast early and the pace collapses, opening a clear final-furlong lane for closers.
scenarios.body: Safari Dream is the most credible hold-up beneficiary given its three course-distance wins and Finley Marsh's tactical experience, though a modest tempo makes this genuinely unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a uniformly even tempo and the field fans out, producing a messy short-head finish across the whole group.
scenarios.body: Pull The Rug and Alkuwarrior, both displaced from their natural hold-up positions and carrying STYLE_FIT/REDISTRIBUTED caveats, would need a fluke of pace and gaps to land this shape — structurally the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sixtygeesbaby has the run of the race if allowed a soft lead — watch whether Liosa attempts to go with it from the gates, as any early challenge fundamentally changes the pace dynamic and opens the race up for hold-up types.

Army Bugler steps up to 6f having been beaten a short-head at the trip last time — watch how Harry Vigors positions it in the first furlong; if it tracks Sixtygeesbaby closely, it becomes the most dangerous finisher in the field.

Safari Dream's late-run profile is entirely dependent on a stronger-than-expected early tempo — if the early fractions are slow (likely with an uncontested leader), Finley Marsh will have a tactical decision to make about whether to press forward sooner than ideal.

Pull The Rug and Alkuwarrior are both carrying REDISTRIBUTED/STYLE_FIT flags, meaning neither is truly racing in its optimal position — if either makes an unexpected forward move early, it signals a change in race shape worth noting for in-play purposes.

races.name: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sofian
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with two recent Good-ground placings at 8f, dropping back to 7½f which may be on the sharp side; Kieran O'Neill rides for Nikki Evans whose 14-day record is modest, and Sofian will need genuine pace to reel in the leader from deep.|
runners_data.comment: Sofian shaped with promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while his ranking of second among these seven runners suggests he holds strong claims — the refusal last time is the one factor to keep onside.

runners_data.name: Searchingtheblues
runners_data.note: Headgear (p) noted and trainer Mark Usher fires on a strong 14-day strike rate (1/12); however, 35 days off and a form string including several double-digit finishes at this trip on similar going make it hard to be enthused — a hold-up type who needs real gallop that is unlikely to materialise here.|
runners_data.comment: Searchingtheblues bounced back to claim third two starts back and, having run over today's trip and going, she arrives with solid fitness after 35 days off, but winless in recent starts is the concern she must overcome from stall seven off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and primary pace-setter; Rod Millman's yard has been quiet (0/19 in 14 days) but Cypriot Diaspora has placed on Good ground twice in her last five, knows her job thoroughly, and facing no rivals willing to press her she can control tempo entirely to suit herself.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts but consistently placed in her two most recent outings, Cypriot Diaspora arrives on a sharp 17-day turnaround with distance and going experience in her favour; the risk is that she has struggled to convert that consistency into a win.

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good ground and has placed twice in similar conditions, making her the hold-up horse with the most relevant form profile here; she is a natural rear-runner who has been mapped closer than her instinct because the field is saturated with hold-up types, so her chance is partly contingent on whether she settles comfortably in an unnatural position.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to boost her claims here, and she has run over today's trip and going before; however, a patchy recent record in her last five starts and 133 lb to carry may work against her, leaving her a competitive but not clear-cut proposition from stall four.

runners_data.name: Oviedo
runners_data.note: Alexandra Dunn has a sharp 14-day record (1/1) and Millie Wonnacott's claim helps at the weights; the "fades in finish" flag is a concern, and while her most recent win came at 8f on Good ground, she has been badly beaten at this trip before — a hold-up runner now shown in midfield who carries a Style_Fit discount.|
runners_data.comment: Oviedo won last time out and returns quickly on a nine-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; drawn in stall one carrying 129 lb, he rates as the one to beat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Green Icon
runners_data.note: Nine consecutive Good-ground runs without a win, including multiple low-finishes at this exact trip, paint a difficult picture; carries "fades in finish" and Style_Fit concerns together, and William Carson's booking for a trainer on 1/11 form over 14 days does little to lift confidence in a horse not racing in its preferred role.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Green Icon makes for a difficult fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a manageable 36-day break carrying 128 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Ravenglass
runners_data.note: Headgear (b) and a course-relevant 2nd at 7f on Good ground give Ravenglass a degree of course-and-distance credibility; Joe Leavy partners a horse whose natural hold-up style is compressed inward by the field shape, though four places in last five runs shows consistency if conditions click — the Style_Fit tag is the key caveat.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Ravenglass faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and arrives on a reasonable 36-day break carrying 126 lb from stall two, with a second three starts back offering a crumb of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Cypriot Diaspora is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven and should lead unchallenged from the gates, setting a sustainable, controlled tempo over 7½ furlongs on good ground at Ffos Las. With no rival likely to contest the lead aggressively, Jack Doughty can dictate fractions from the front and effectively turn this into a test of who can pick him off in the straight rather than a gruelling pace battle. The remainder of the field — Kaleidoscope Eyes, Green Icon, Ravenglass, Oviedo, Sofian, and Searchingtheblues — are all hold-up or midfield types, meaning there will be a significant cluster of horses hunting Cypriot Diaspora from behind rather than racing alongside her. This shape strongly favours a horse who can travel close enough to the leader to land a telling blow early in the straight, rather than a deep closer who needs a truly searching pace to reel the leader in — with the tempo set to be modest and uncontested, a genuinely prominent-to-midfield profile that can close from a length or two back holds the advantage over pure hold-up runners needing maximum pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cypriot Diaspora Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cypriot Diaspora leads at a comfortable, uncontested clip and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap early enough in the straight.
scenarios.body: Cypriot Diaspora dictates a measured tempo, conserves energy through the race, and quickens away from a chasing bunch that is shuffled wide and too far back to reel her in; on good turf where front-runners who set honest fractions are rewarded, her recent Good-ground placing record supports this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling second or third just off Cypriot Diaspora's pace makes smooth headway from two furlongs out and collars her near the line.
scenarios.body: With the pace set by one front-runner and the bulk of the field grouped behind, the horse best positioned to travel on the coat-tails of the leader has a short, direct run at the prize; Kaleidoscope Eyes has the most relevant Good-ground win form and could sit close enough to pounce despite being a natural hold-up type pushed forward in this configuration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected or Cypriot Diaspora ties up inside the final furlong, leaving a gap for a genuine deep closer.
scenarios.body: A sustained gallop from the front would play into the hands of a horse held up for a late run, but with only one pace-setter and five genuine hold-up types all needing a strong tempo, this scenario relies on conditions that are unlikely to materialise without a rival pressing Cypriot Diaspora early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Muddled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race, runners switch wide simultaneously, and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A compressed finish would be chaotic in a field where multiple hold-up types are all searching for clear daylight in the straight; a horse with a sharp turn of foot who finds a gap quickly would benefit, but with Style_Fit concerns across several runners, confidence in any one beneficiary is low.

watchPoints.text: Cypriot Diaspora is uncontested in front — watch whether Jack Doughty allows the fractions to drop dangerously slow, which could make her almost impossible to catch from the rear two furlongs out.

Five genuine hold-up types (Kaleidoscope Eyes, Ravenglass, Oviedo, Green Icon, Sofian) will all be hunting the same ground in the straight — watch for traffic congestion and wide-tracking from two furlongs out that could cost several runners dearly.

Kaleidoscope Eyes carries a Style_Fit score of 0.94, meaning she is racing out of her natural deep-closer role — watch whether Robbie Downey attempts to push forward early to compensate, which could unsettle her settling pattern.

Both Oviedo (9d) and Ravenglass (36d) are on opposite ends of the freshness spectrum — watch whether the recent runner (Oviedo) shows sharpness from the gate or the freshened-up Ravenglass travels with more zest through the race.

Green Icon's form shows repeated near-last finishes on Good ground at this trip specifically — watch market moves; any significant support would suggest connections have found something the form book has not.

races.name: Ascona Ladies In Lace Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner for Sir Mark Prescott with six runs of form all showing leads pressed into second placings; the uncontested lead on Good at 7½f is a career-best scenario, and Luke Morris is an astute judge of pace — 25 days since last run is no concern for this stable.

runners_data.name: Likeness
runners_data.note: Returned a solid 2nd on her last Good-ground start at 7f and Jack Channon's runner is 138 days absent, which adds a fitness question; as a hold-up type she will naturally settle last, but in a three-runner field that position is barely a length off the pace — her best hope is that the leaders crack late.

runners_data.name: Reader
runners_data.note: Showed two placed efforts on Good going from three relevant runs, and Marcus Tregoning's horse profiles as a prominent tracker who will sit directly behind Korbut throughout; Jack Doughty keeps it simple in small fields, and the 6f-to-7½f step up looks manageable given the two 8f runs in her history.

races.paceDynamic: Korbut is the sole confirmed front-runner in a three-horse field and will lead from the gates unchallenged, setting a sustainable, owner-controlled tempo over 7½f at Ffos Las on Good ground. Reader will sit in a prominent tracking position just off Korbut's heels, while Likeness — a hold-up type — will be anchored at the rear of the tiny field, effectively just a length or two off the pace in a race this small. With no pressure applied to Korbut, the pace will be honest but not punishing, meaning the leader can conserve energy through the middle portions and still have something left for the run-in. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles: a gentle gallop with a clear leader dictating suits Korbut directly, and Reader — tracking closely throughout — is ideally placed to pounce; Likeness must find an extra gear from a position that in a three-runner race offers no real tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Korbut Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Korbut leads at a comfortable tempo and retains enough in reserve to quicken when challenged in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Korbut's consistent record of front-running in similar-going conditions at 7f trips means this is entirely within his comfort zone, and an uncontested lead over 7½f on Good turf is the ideal setup for his style. The small field removes any risk of a rival forcing a suicidal pace, so Korbut can control every yard and arrive at the two-furlong pole with energy to burn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Reader Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Reader tracks Korbut closely throughout and produces a sustained challenge from the two-furlong marker to wear down the leader.
scenarios.body: Reader has shown smart form on Good ground (3rd and 2nd from three Good-going runs) and the prominent tracking role in a small field means minimal ground is wasted throughout the race. A lack of a true strong gallop can expose a front-runner late, and Reader's closer proximity suits this scenario best.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Likeness Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Korbut ties up in the final furlong, allowing Likeness to reel in the field from the back.
scenarios.body: In a three-runner race, Likeness has almost no positional disadvantage, but as a genuine hold-up horse she still needs rivals to come back to her rather than quickening away. Her 138-day absence and limited recent form make this the least reliable scenario, requiring both a career-best performance and significant leader capitulation.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If any horse is slow from the gates or the early order becomes confused, creating an uncharacteristically irregular gallop pattern.
scenarios.body: With only three runners there is very little scope for positional chaos, and Korbut's consistent gate-to-wire profile makes a truly scrambled race unlikely. This scenario is included only for completeness and would most benefit whichever horse adapts quickest to an unexpected tempo shift.

watchPoints.text: Korbut's finishing effort — his form shows a string of 2nds when pressed, so watch whether Luke Morris has enough horse to hold Reader's late challenge inside the final furlong.
Likeness's fitness after 138 days off; if she shows any signs of blowing early or lacking her usual kick, she becomes a non-factor in what is already a three-runner contest.
Reader's jockey Jack Doughty should look to keep Reader tight on Korbut's heels from the outset — any daylight allowed in a three-runner race could prove decisive given the slow-burn pace.
Track bias check: all three races run so far today at Ffos Las at this trip have returned Good, confirming a consistent surface — no rail or ground advantage likely to distort the result.

races.name: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly from Edward Smyth-Osbourne's yard with no wins or places on good ground in her six similar-going starts; stepping up to 7½f for the first time and Harry Vigors (5) has limited opportunities to shine from the back in an unpressured gallop.
runners_data.comment: Medyg has run over today's trip and arrives here 25 days fresh, with our rating of 63 suggesting he holds more ability than his official mark of 55 implies — the main concern is a sequence of modest finishes in recent starts that he must reverse.

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's filly carries strong placed form in good-ground races at 7f and 8f (4 places from 11 similar-going runs), making her the most credible hold-up runner if the pace does set up for closers; quick turnaround at 9 days is worth monitoring but O'Meara excels on this type of target.
runners_data.comment: Willowinghurn is our top-rated, and returns fit just nine days after her last start, has run over today's trip and going before, and carries 135 lb from stall two; the risk is a winless recent spell that makes her hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Lady Fizz
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the finish which is a real concern when the pace may be modest and the closing stages become a sprint; one placed run from four on good ground and this is as competitive a field as she has met on the all-weather.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Lady Fizz faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a handy 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Gal
runners_data.note: A genuine closer by nature though mapped to midfield here given the surplus of hold-up types; her best form came winning a 7f good-ground race (1W2P from 5 similar-going outings) and if she can travel prominently she has the most meaningful recent winning profile in the field.
runners_data.comment: Gal won two starts back and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround having already experienced today's trip and conditions, with our rating of 65 suggesting she holds more ability than her official mark implies. The risk is her last run — an eighth — which she must bounce back from.

runners_data.name: Iconic Dawn
runners_data.note: Blinkers noted; Morrison's filly has placed three times at 8f on good ground but tends to find a few too many in front of her, and Gina Mangan rides; the 7½f trip is within range but she has not shown a sharp enough turn of foot to win off a slow tempo.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Iconic Dawn at least has experience of today's trip and going to draw on, and a fourth last time out suggests some return to form, though she must do better from stall eight carrying 132 lb off an official mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Golden Mabel
runners_data.note: Lisa Williamson's filly has been a consistent finisher without winning from eight good-ground starts; she runs here out of her preferred deep hold-up position which reduces her chance of producing a decisive finish, and headgear (hood) has not unlocked a win yet.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with finishes no better than fifth in recent starts, Golden Mabel faces a stiff task on these figures, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 13 days.

runners_data.name: Diamond Ali
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and the key pace-maker; she won over 8f on soft ground and ran well fresh, and the 74-day break needs monitoring, but Carson knows how to use a soft lead and her prior placed form at 7f on good ground keeps her in the picture throughout.
runners_data.comment: Diamond Ali bounced back to form with a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him well-suited on paper; the 74-day break is the one query, but that recent victory gives him solid claims from stall five carrying 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Cougar Force
runners_data.note: George Bass rides a natural closer who has placed twice at 6f on good ground; she steps up to 7½f here for the first time (last run at 8f was 13th) and at 87 days since last racing is the least match-fit runner in the field — her true style is rear-running but the field shape forces her to a midfield role.
runners_data.comment: Cougar Force arrives winless in her last five starts, though third last time out offers a crumb of comfort, and she has experience of today's going; the 87-day absence and a rating of 47 suggest she faces a stiff task from stall seven carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Follow My Heart
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's consistent filly has shown placed form at 5f and 6f on good ground in her most recent runs; she is pushed into a midfield position here despite being a natural closer, and the step up to 7½f is unproven territory — Ryan Kavanagh (3) will need a smooth passage.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and again three starts back, Follow My Heart has shown consistency without a win in recent starts, and experience over today's trip and going lends quiet appeal; a 31-day break and 126 lb from stall four are the key variables to weigh.

runners_data.name: Arvana Belle
runners_data.note: Millman's other runner has the most impressive good-ground record of the hold-up types here — a win and three places from 10 good-ground starts including a win at 7f; Jack Doughty takes the mount and she brings the most consistent placed form at this sort of trip, though she races here out of her natural sweeping hold-up role.
runners_data.comment: Arvana Belle arrives on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going in her favour, and a third three starts back offers some encouragement; yet she remains winless in her last six starts, and a rating of 45 underlines the uphill task from draw 3.

runners_data.name: Independent Angel
runners_data.note: Williamson's second runner shows most of her form at 5f and 6f, making the 7½f trip a real query; she has not placed on good ground in five attempts and Millie Wonnacott (5) will need everything to fall perfectly for this outsider to feature from a redistributed midfield slot.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Independent Angel is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a sharp 12-day turnaround at least fit.

runners_data.name: Kaiko
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just three runs, all at 6f and 8f on fast or good ground with no placed form; Adrian Wintle's filly faces a tough task stepping into this competitive handicap and Finley Marsh will need a significant step forward from a runner still finding her feet at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kaiko faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns on a reasonable 21-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Ali is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press her, William Carson can dictate terms at a comfortable, sustainable clip across the 7½ furlongs on good ground at Ffos Las. The field behind her is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Gal, Golden Mabel, Cougar Force, Follow My Heart, Arvana Belle, Independent Angel and Kaiko are all natural closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many of them to occupy the rear — meaning the pack will likely settle in a compressed bunch, dependent on a strong pace to generate the momentum they need. At 7½ furlongs on a flat course with a single honest gallop-setter, the tempo is unlikely to be genuinely testing, which reduces the chance of late closers producing a devastating finishing burst off the home turn. This race shape favours a horse able to race prominently or make an early challenge from a handy position, as the unpressured lead means Diamond Ali could dictate and the finishers may not get the sustained strong pace they need to reel her in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diamond Ali Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Ali is allowed to bowl along at a fair but uncontested pace and Carson controls the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She gets a soft lead, settles her rhythm through the first half and still has something in reserve to repel challengers in the closing stages; no horse naturally bred to front-run can put her under early pressure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Challenges Home Turn
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse moves prominently from early and applies pressure to Diamond Ali from the three-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The steadier early gallop means a horse who travels well just off the pace can arrive on Diamond Ali's quarters with momentum still in hand; Gal's win form on good ground at 7f makes her the most dangerous in this shape despite her redistribution.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and create a late-running opportunity.
scenarios.body: This is less likely given the lone pace-setter and compressed midfield, but if Carson over-commits and the field fragments, hold-up types tracking wide could benefit; Willowinghurn's solid record in similar going and Iconic Dawn's placed form at this trip give them residual claims.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Bunched Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace causes the entire field to bunch and the race turns into a six-furlong dash for home.
scenarios.body: With no pace injection until late, position in the straight becomes critical and a horse drawn wide or unable to get a run through a wall of rivals is at a severe disadvantage; Follow My Heart and Cougar Force, who both show placed form in similar conditions, have the profile to thread through.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Ali (William Carson) gets away cleanly and dictates — if she is allowed a clear uncontested lead through the first three furlongs, she becomes very difficult to peg back at 7½f with a modest gallop.

Gal is shown in midfield but is a genuine hold-up runner by nature — watch where Luke Morris actually positions her at the start; if she can travel handy, her good-ground win form at 7f makes her a live danger to the leader.

The large cluster of redistributed closers — Cougar Force, Follow My Heart, Arvana Belle, Independent Angel, Kaiko — may cause significant traffic congestion on the home turn if the field remains bunched behind a single slow pace-setter; any horse wide or blocked at the two-furlong pole is at serious risk.

Cougar Force has not run for 87 days and Diamond Ali for 74 days — both runners returning from a break of over two months in a competitive 12-runner handicap; market moves for either would carry extra significance given the fitness query.

Willowinghurn runs just nine days after her last start for David O'Meara whose 14-day strike rate of 8/52 confirms he targets quick-turnaround runners — watch for confidence in the market as a sign the yard believes she is cherry-ripe.

races.name: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 8f on Good, but stepping up sharply to 1m2f for the first time in this field; a natural hold-up horse who will likely find herself further from the action than ideal in a race with little genuine pace to close into, and Ben Ffrench Davis (5lb claim) takes some of the weight concern away without solving the tactical problem.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, A Rose Adaay faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 12 days, suggesting she is fit.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Placed in two 1m2f Good-ground races recently — trip and going both stack up well for Ian Williams' mare; wears tongue strap and will be ridden hold-up by Joe Leavy, but in a field dominated by closers she may struggle to find clear daylight at the business end unless she positions herself more forwardly than her style suggests.
runners_data.comment: Charencey has been in fine nick of late, finishing third last time out and a runner-up in each of his two starts before that, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: City Escape
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has been running in 1m2f+ company consistently, though a string of five-to-six finishes paints a clear picture; her /es headgear and natural tendency to race at the rear mean she needs race conditions to play out very differently to what this pace map projects, and Kieran O'Neill faces a stiff task finding cover and a late run.
runners_data.comment: City Escape has run over today's trip and going, rates 8 lb above her official mark on our figures, and 28 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; the main risk is that she has been winless in her last five starts, with nothing better than fifth to show.

runners_data.name: Gert Lush
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's veteran has placed five times in her last fifteen runs on Good ground and her record over 1m+ trips is solid; Gina Mangan keeps the ride and the mare has the profile of a horse who can adapt her position slightly — the 1m2f trip here represents a good opportunity if the race develops into a two-furlong dash.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Gert Lush nonetheless brings solid recent consistency with a second last time out and a third two starts back, and she has experience over today's distance and going; 135 lb from stall nine is the challenge to overcome.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's 7-year-old wears blinkers and has placed three times in fifteen recent starts, though those wins have mainly come over shorter; Donagh Murphy (7lb) on board, and though the horse is a genuine hold-up type, the step up to 1m2f with limited evidence at the trip means there is a query over whether he truly stays, compounding the pace-map disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, King Of The Dance nonetheless showed promise with a third two runs back, though an unseated last time out clouds his current form; he has distance and going experience to call on, and carrying 135 lb from stall two, he merits respect as a midfield prospect.

runners_data.name: Prophet Squeeze
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy runner wearing a hood who has returned pulled up and refused on recent starts — a serious form concern before any tactical considerations; Christian Howarth (3lb) claims and the horse has zero wins or places at this trip on Good going, making it very difficult to construct a winning scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a refused to race among them and multiple seventh-place finishes, Prophet Squeeze faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 24 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but her figures make her very hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Racing Demon
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles' six-year-old has placed four times in fifteen outings and ran second over 8f on Good; wears a hood and Luke Morris is an astute jockey who may push for a more prominent position than the horse's typical style, which would be the key to unlocking a better result in a race with a moderate pace.
runners_data.comment: Racing Demon shapes as a leading threat on our rating of 58, ranking him second in the field, and he arrives fit on 21 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going; the main risk is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Strong Man Tom
runners_data.note: Worrying profile — the horse is flagged as fading in finishes and has not placed in recent outings over 8-10f; Ryan Kavanagh (3lb) takes the claim but Barry John Murphy's low strike rate and the horse's tendency to be beaten well before the line makes this a very hard race to win regardless of pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Strong Man Tom faces a stiff task here; he has shown little in recent outings, though 28 days off at least suggests connections have had time to work on him.

runners_data.name: Typeface
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has a strong 14-day record and Harry Vigors (5lb) partners the 4-year-old who has won twice and placed five times in recent form; wears a hood, has solid Good-ground form at 10f, and crucially could be one of the more adaptable hold-up types willing to travel handily — the strongest overall profile in the race.
runners_data.comment: Typeface has been knocking on the door with back-to-back thirds in his most recent starts, and with experience over today's trip and going, the top-rated runner here looks the one to side with, even if a win continues to elude him.

runners_data.name: Elora Prince
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's three-year-old is running off a 128lb weight and carries the benefit of youth, but six recent outings show only declining form figures since debut; Finley Marsh has the mount and the horse has placed just once in fourteen runs on Good, making it hard to see where the improvement comes from in this competitive context.
runners_data.comment: Elora Prince has run over today's trip and going before, but he arrives winless in his last six starts with finishes no better than fourth, and while a fourth two starts back offers a shade of encouragement, the gelding must find more to make a serious impact from stall five carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Lapidarist
runners_data.note: David Simcock's three-year-old is a natural prominent racer redistributed to the front by necessity — placed twice over 10f and ran second twice in recent form, suggesting a willing frontrunner who could get loose on the lead; Taryn Langley (5lb) is less experienced at dictating, and if the horse is allowed to bowl along unanswered the tactical advantage of the lead on Good ground over 1m2f is a genuine asset.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Lapidarist nonetheless shows consistency with two runner-up finishes in recent form, and has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 128 lb from stall four, she holds claims but her tendency to fill the minor positions without converting is the concern.

races.paceDynamic: Lapidarist is the sole mapped front-runner here, though this is a redistribution — the horse is a natural prominent type that will likely find itself on or near the lead simply through a lack of genuine pace in the race. With no confirmed front-runner to push proceedings, Lapidarist should set a relaxed, measured tempo over 1m2f on Good turf at Ffos Las, dictating a strongly-run finish only if rivals choose to challenge. The overwhelming majority of this field are true hold-up types — Charencey, City Escape, King Of The Dance, Prophet Squeeze, Elora Prince, and Strong Man Tom are all natural rearward runners compressed into midfield positions on the map because the race cannot accommodate them all at the back. A steady gallop set by Lapidarist will compress the race into a test of finishing speed rather than stamina, significantly favouring those with a clean turn of foot from a handy position; pure closers relying on a strong pace to close into will find conditions less than ideal. The race shape most strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types that can travel close enough to the moderate pace and pick off a tiring Lapidarist in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lapidarist Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Lapidarist goes unchallenged to the front and sets a modest, controlled pace that suits its own finishing effort.
scenarios.body: Lapidarist bowls along in front at a comfortable clip, the large hold-up contingent unable to generate the pace they need to close, and the race develops into a tactical sprint from two furlongs out where the leader has the first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Finisher Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a handy-travelling hold-up horse settles close enough to the moderate pace and produces a decisive finishing kick in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The lack of a true strong pace means a runner who positions themselves in the first four from early on finds themselves perfectly placed when the race quickens, picking off the front-runner without needing to make ground from far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a quicker-than-expected tempo develops and the large hold-up contingent find sufficient gaps to close through in the straight.
scenarios.body: A stronger pace — unlikely given the personnel — would allow true hold-up types like Racing Demon and Charencey to make meaningful late headway, but several redistributed horses in this group are not genuinely suited to coming from last, limiting confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, No Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses attempt to force a prominent position early, creating scrimmaging and an unpredictably messy tempo.
scenarios.body: Interference and positional jostling in the early stages leaves the race unsettled, with no horse able to dominate, producing a scrambled finish where course form and adaptability matter most.

watchPoints.text: Typeface and Gert Lush are the two most likely winners if the race unfolds as a moderate-pace tactical affair — watch whether Harry Vigors or Gina Mangan commit to a more forward position than their horses' typical style would suggest.

Lapidarist holds all the early cards as the sole pace-setter, but Taryn Langley (5lb claimer) dictating from the front is an inexperience risk — monitor whether any rival challenges for the lead in the first half-mile, which would instantly change the race shape.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses in this race — Charencey, Racing Demon, City Escape, King Of The Dance all seeking the same late ground — means significant traffic congestion is likely in the straight; Joe Leavy and Luke Morris are the most tactically astute jockeys to navigate it.

Prophet Squeeze's recent form figures (R and 9) are a significant safety flag — connections should be monitored at the start and in the preliminary stages given the pulled-up run within the last six outings.

races.name: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up performer who has won and placed on Good ground at distances beyond 1m4f, giving him the stamina credentials to be competitive here; Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) reduces the 135lb burden slightly, and 52 days since last run is not a concern given his recent placed effort at this trip on Good.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and third again four starts back, Cogital shows enough consistency in recent starts to appeal here, and he returns fresh after 52 days with experience of today's trip and conditions — winless in his last five, but the overall profile makes him our pick.

runners_data.name: Virtual Hug
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old in fair form with a recent win at 1m2f on Good, though her true tactic is to race from behind — she will find herself drawn into midfield rather than her preferred deep-closing berth given how many hold-up types are in this field, which blunts her optimal chance.|
runners_data.comment: Virtual Hug brings solid fitness on 24 days' absence and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, with a win and a third in recent starts giving him a live each-way profile; the worry is he has finished fourth in three of his last six starts, suggesting consistency remains the risk.

runners_data.name: Buck Barrow
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with back-to-back placed efforts at 1m2f on Good and a win on Soft, so the ground and trip suit; trainer Wintle landed one winner from five in the past 14 days suggesting stable in decent form, though his natural rear-racing style is compromised by field composition — he will race closer to the pace than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Buck Barrow catches the eye as one of the highest-rated runners in the field, arriving in solid nick with consecutive thirds last two outings and a win three starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and conditions; the concern is that his official mark of 51 leaves him shouldering 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Master Dancer
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose recent form includes a third at 1m2f on Soft and a Flat Stalls flag on headgear, but his sim-going record shows no wins and only one place from 15 similar-ground runs, suggesting the conditions are not his friend; his hold-up style is further constrained by redistribution to midfield.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Master Dancer does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third three starts back shows he can find the frame; however, that eighth last time out after a 46-day break, combined with a lowly official mark of 50, leaves him hard to enthuse over.

runners_data.name: Adrian
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has placed twice at 1m6f on Soft and has a second at 1m2f on Soft, so handles Give underfoot, but with a sim-going record of just two Good appearances (one placing) his form on today's surface is thin; 78 days off the track adds an element of rust, and his natural deep-closing style is crowded out by the field shape.|
runners_data.comment: Adrian shaped with promise when second last time out, and he has experience of today's distance and going to call upon; winless in his last five starts is the concern, as is the 78-day absence.

runners_data.name: Atalanta Mist
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old with five consecutive top-three finishes including placed efforts on Good at 1m2f, stepping up to 1m4f for the first time today; Marcus Tregoning's stable placed one from six in the past fortnight, and the unexposed stamina profile at this trip makes her an interesting participant in the staying division.|
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts — third last time out, and a placed effort in four of her last five — Atalanta Mist has experience of today's trip and going, though 44 days off the track and a mark of 53 leave her with something to prove.

runners_data.name: Saxophonic
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a warning flag for fading in the finish, backed by only one sim-going run (placed) from seven attempts; the step up to 1m4f is unproven and David Simcock's stable has had no winners from eight runs in the past 14 days — a hold-up type who needs conditions to be just right.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Saxophonic at least has experience over today's trip and a modest 29-day turnaround keeping him fresh, though a fourth last time out and a string of modest efforts before that suggest he faces a stiff ask from 126 lb off a mark of 52.

runners_data.name: Dream Of Ithaca
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field, she won over 1m2f on Good last time and gets to operate completely unopposed on the front end here; the STYLE_FIT tag notes she is mapped slightly out of her natural role as a prominent racer, but in this field she effectively becomes the lone pace-setter, which is a significant positional advantage at Ffos Las.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten in three of her last four starts before winning last time out, Dream Of Ithaca arrives on a quick turnaround but that victory is the solitary bright spot in a patchy recent spell, and a rating of 49 ranked eighth of ten makes her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Emerald Reine
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old with three runs all resulting in seventh, eighth and ninth on Soft or Standard — no Good-ground form on record and a sim-going stat of one from three appearances; her natural hold-up style is further diluted by redistribution, and the form profile offers little encouragement at this stage of her development.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Emerald Reine has tumbled down the field on each recent outing and 86 days off the track adds a fitness query, though she has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Beau Chevalier
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a finishing-fade flag and a form string entirely composed of double-figure and mid-field efforts on Good and Standard, all at 7f-8f — stepping up significantly in trip to 1m4f represents a major stamina unknown; only 12 days between runs suggests connections are hopeful, but the evidence is not supportive.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Beau Chevalier faces a stiff task, though a 12-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh and the 119 lb burden is at least manageable.

races.paceDynamic: Dream Of Ithaca is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, she will control tempo from the outset at Ffos Las on Good turf. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly held-up in style — Cogital, Virtual Hug, Buck Barrow, Master Dancer, Adrian, Atalanta Mist, Saxophonic, Emerald Reine and Beau Chevalier all prefer to race off the pace — meaning Dream Of Ithaca can dictate a genuinely comfortable, uncontested gallop and control every gear change. At 1m4f on Good ground this creates a race shape where the leader can conserve energy through the first mile and potentially stretch clear before the closers summon sufficient momentum, especially if the pace is only moderate. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically obtain their ideal deep-closing position, with Virtual Hug, Buck Barrow, Master Dancer, Adrian and Beau Chevalier all redistributed from their natural rear-most berths into a congested midfield pack — of those, Buck Barrow and Virtual Hug, with recent form at this trip, are most likely to navigate through and find cleaner air. This race shape decisively favours either Dream Of Ithaca front-running to a controlled victory, or the one or two hold-up horses best-placed in midfield (Cogital, Atalanta Mist) who can track closer than usual and pounce without needing to make up excessive ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dream Of Ithaca Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Of Ithaca sets a measured, uncontested pace and quickens at the two-furlong pole before hold-up horses can organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: With no pressure through the first mile on Good ground, she dictates every fraction and her rivals — strung out in a congested hold-up pack — are unable to synchronise a meaningful late surge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Chasers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sustainable enough to set up a finish but the hold-up horses best-positioned in midfield close on the final bend.
scenarios.body: Cogital's proven Good-ground form at extended distances and Atalanta Mist's consistent placed form at 1m2f-1m4f on Good make them the likeliest beneficiaries as they track closer than their natural style, bridging the gap in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Hold-Ups Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Of Ithaca sets a strong enough tempo to bring genuine late closers into it from the rear of the midfield pack.
scenarios.body: Virtual Hug and Buck Barrow, both proven at this trip on Good ground, would need a fast-run race to make their best form count, but their redistribution to midfield means they are unlikely to secure ideal ground off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Of Ithaca's fractions are so slow that the entire field effectively races as one unit turning for home.
scenarios.body: A sprint-finish scenario at 1m4f would expose Saxophonic and Beau Chevalier's tendency to fade in the closing stages, but Atalanta Mist's consistent placed form suggests she handles a muddling gallop better than most.

watchPoints.text: Dream Of Ithaca is the only horse likely to lead and could use the uncontested pace to steal an unassailable advantage — watch whether any rider attempts to pressure her in the early stages, as a true solo lead at 1m4f on Good could prove decisive.

The midfield pack is artificially congested with redistributed hold-up types (Virtual Hug, Buck Barrow, Master Dancer, Adrian, Beau Chevalier) — watch for traffic problems and interference in the straight as eight horses converge on a narrow racing line at Ffos Las.

Cogital's jockey Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) is riding for trainer Bernard Llewellyn who has no wins from seven runners in the past 14 days — watch whether the inexperience of a claiming jockey in a tactical 1m4f race allows Dream Of Ithaca to build too large a lead.

Atalanta Mist is unraced beyond 1m2f and steps up in trip for the first time — watch how Jack Doughty positions her through the first mile, as an unexposed stayer could improve markedly or find the extra distance beyond her current stamina limit.

Saxophonic and Beau Chevalier both carry finishing-fade flags — if the pace is slow and the race develops into a sprint finish from two furlongs out, watch both horses closely as they are statistically likely to drop away when the pressure comes.
